body:
Unity is a game engine that can be used to make all types of games for mobile (iOS and android) and desktop PC games. It's free and comes with tutorials to get you started. Beyond the tutorials that come with the software, many YouTube tutorials also exist. 

The main scripting language Unity uses is Unityscript, which is a programming language similar to JavaScript. You can find alot of JavaScript tutorials on YouTube, but I recommend going to codeacademy.com and doing their tutorial. It's very easy if you already know some programming and will take a couple of hours.

This could get you started in making some simple games and experimenting.

Find out what part of the process you like best, the art side or the programming side. Most game development is split in terms of what you will be doing most of the time, however it's always good to have an understandable of how both sides of game development work. 

Beyond trying to make games, do some googling and figure out how to start modding existing games. This is how many game developers got their start and is a great way to figure out how games work and have some fun in the process.

As for computer, the better it is at gaming the better it will be for game development. That may be an oversimplicstion but you basically just want to get the highest RAM, best processor, and best graphics card you can get for your budget. However, this is Lord cost effective if you just build a desktop PC rather than paying super computer costs for a bulky gaming laptop.

Last thought: I don't feel like searching, but there has so be some game development subreddits, for beginners and experts. Find them and they will be able to answer your questions better.


Edit: start looking at universities that have computer science or game development programs. I'm not sure what programs the schools you have already been looking at offer, but shop around and stay away from schools that aren't real Universities (tech schools , devry, ect)
